display.title: Tu B'Shvat: Rosh Hashanah for the Trees
display.summary_short: Why Tu B'Shvat is the New Year for trees, which fruits we eat and which brachos we say, and how our good deeds are our own fruits.
display.summary_long: A short Tu B'Shvat talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi asks how Rosh Hashanah can be only five months after Tishrei, and explains that the Mishnah lists several new years, among them the Rosh Hashanah for trees on the fifteenth of Shevat, when the trees in Eretz Yisroel begin to blossom. We celebrate by eating the fruits for which the Torah praises Eretz Yisroel: wheat, barley, grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives and dates. We say Borei Pri Ha'etz, and Shehecheyanu on a fruit eaten for the first time that year; some save carob or pomegranates all year for this. The Torah compares a person to a tree of the field: just as a tree is praised for its fruit, our fruits are our mitzvos and good deeds, so Tu B'Shvat is a time for resolutions to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos. He ends with a prayer to celebrate next Tu B'Shvat in Eretz Yisroel with Moshiach.
display.lesson: A person is like a tree: our good deeds are our fruits, so make resolutions to grow in Torah and mitzvos.
